terms.definition: The post-Civil War process of restoring the Union and redefining freedom and citizenship.
The amendment establishing birthright citizenship, due process, and equal protection.
The amendment prohibiting voting discrimination based on race, color, or previous servitude.
A federal agency supporting formerly enslaved people and war refugees.
An agricultural labor system in which tenants paid landowners with a share of crops.
Land designated by the federal government for Native nations, often through coercive policy.
Division of communally held tribal land into individual parcels under federal policy.
A federal law offering western land to eligible settlers who met conditions.
An African American migrant who moved from the South to the West after Reconstruction.
A postwar vision of a diversified, industrializing southern economy.
A legally recognized organization that can own property, enter contracts, and limit investor liability.
Dominant control of a market by one firm or coordinated group.
Control of multiple stages of production and distribution.
Negotiation between workers and employers through representatives.
Organized refusal to work in order to press demands.
A system of laws and customs enforcing racial segregation and white supremacy.
The removal or obstruction of voting rights.
A tax used in some states as a condition for voting.
A late nineteenth-century movement seeking political and economic reform for farmers and workers.
An organization that exchanges services or patronage for political support.
A diverse reform movement seeking responses to industrial and urban problems.
A journalist who investigated corruption or harmful conditions.
A process allowing voters to propose laws.
A direct vote on a proposed law or policy.
A process for removing an elected official before the end of a term.
